blurb: Tall, rough-coated Scottish sighthound once used to course red deer in the Highlands
description: The Scottish Deerhound is a very tall British sighthound, bred to course red deer, with a harsh grey coat and a build like a larger, heavier-boned Greyhound.
answer: The Scottish Deerhound, or simply Deerhound, is a large sighthound from Scotland, once bred to hunt red deer by coursing. It looks like a bigger, heavier-boned Greyhound with a rough coat. It is one of the tallest sighthounds, standing about 71 to 76 cm or more.

body: The breed became widely known as the Scottish Deerhound in the early 19th century and was the main foundation breed of the modern Irish Wolfhound in the late 19th century. Single dogs or pairs were released to run down red deer by speed. As estates were split up and slower tracking dogs came into favour with modern rifles, the breed declined towards 1900 and survived through a few enthusiasts who made it a show breed.

The breed standard asks for males of at least 30 inches weighing about 39 to 50 kg, and females from 28 inches weighing about 34 to 43 kg. The harsh coat is 3 to 4 inches long, with a softer beard and moustache. Modern dogs come only in shades of grey, blue-grey preferred; older colours such as brindle and red fawn are now lost. The small, dark ears fold back, and the long tail almost reaches the ground.
The source text says little about temperament at home. Historically Deerhounds were valued as fast and silent hunters, and on rough or heavy ground they can outrun a Greyhound.
Sources give little specific detail on care. As a large, fast sighthound it is generally thought to need room to run.

A 2024 UK study found a life expectancy of 10.5 years, compared to 12.7 for purebreds. A UK breed club survey found heart-related causes behind nearly a quarter of deaths and cancer behind 18%. Conditions reported in the breed include dilated cardiomyopathy; one American study found it in 6% of Deerhounds, the highest of any breed.

faq.q: How big does a Scottish Deerhound get?
faq.a: Males are at least 30 inches tall and weigh about 39 to 50 kg; females are from 28 inches and about 34 to 43 kg.

faq.q: What is the difference between a Deerhound and a Greyhound?
faq.a: The Deerhound is larger and more heavily boned, with a rough coat. It is slower on smooth ground but can outrun a Greyhound on rough terrain.

faq.q: Is the Deerhound recognised by the FCI?
faq.a: Yes. It is FCI breed number 164 in Group 10, Sighthounds.
